files.title: File:Antelope Creek Masonry Arch Bridge Mitchell Co KS arch detail.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption: The arch stones are smooth faced except for the keystones, which are rusticated. The stones are finished smooth on the underside of each barrel.

files.title: File:Antelope Creek Masonry Arch Bridge Mitchell Co KS east side.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption: Stone arch bridges and culverts were popular in Kansas for many reasons, a major one being the availability of local stone.

files.title: File:Antelope Creek Masonry Arch Bridge Mitchell Co KS view from road.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption: This bridge was constructed by laborers working under the WPA program. It was constructed in 1940, as documented by a date stone in the bridge rail.

files.title: File:Antelope Creek Masonry Arch Bridge Mitchell Co KS west side wing wall.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption: The stone used for construction of the bridge was mined locally from what is called the Post Rock Limestone Ledge of the Greenhorn Formation. Much of Mitchell County is underlain with the Greenhorn Limestone formation.

files.title: File:Antelope Creek Masonry Arch Bridge Mitchell Co KS wing wall.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption: The stones feature two different finishes, rusticated and smooth. They are laid in an ashlar pattern. There is a course of smooth stones that corresponds to the level of the driving surface and spans the length of the bridge.

files.title: File:Antelope Creek Masonry Arch Bridge Mitchell Co KS.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption: It was built in 1940 as a Work Projects Administration (WPA) project. The bridge is surrounded by pasture land used for grazing and crop fields.
